issues.legal_issue: A pleader entitled to practise in court has the same authority to act for a client as an advocate.
material_facts: The client had engaged a pleader in the civil suit.
The pleader had not enrolled as an advocate but was entitled to practise under the law applicable to pleaders before the Advocates Act came into force.
issues.conclusion: Pleaders and advocates stand on the same footing in their power to act on behalf of clients.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 29 and 55 of the Advocates Act, 1961, support a unified legal profession and preserve the practice rights of pleaders who did not enrol as advocates. Order III, rules 1 and 4, and section 2(15) of the Code of Civil Procedure treat a duly appointed pleader as empowered to act for a party; section 9 of the Bombay Pleaders Act, 1920, also recognises a pleader's authority to appear, plead and act. The Court approved the Full Bench decision in Jiwibai v. Ramjuvar, AIR 1947 Nag. 17, and rejected a status-based distinction between pleaders and advocates.

predicates.legal_practice_authority_case: The proceeding concerns the authority of a legal practitioner to act for a client in court.
predicates.pleader_entitled_to_practise: The pleader was entitled to practise in the court where the proceeding was heard.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a legal practitioner's authority to act and the pleader was entitled to practise in that court, pleaders and advocates have equal authority to act.

issues.legal_issue: An engaged pleader or advocate may compromise a client's case without specific consent only within the limits of the client's instructions, good faith, the client's interests, and a fair opportunity for consultation.
material_facts: The client was not present when the compromise was recorded, but her litigation agent was present and was consulted.
The client had sought several adjournments to settle the suit, and the courts below found that she had not expressly instructed the pleader not to compromise.
The courts below found that the compromise was not a fraud or an act of sharp practice and that the pleader acted bona fide for the client's benefit.
The last hearing was for reporting a compromise; the court refused a further adjournment, and the client was absent.
The compromise gave the client time to deliver possession and set terms for rent arrears, damages and costs.
issues.conclusion: The pleader had implied authority to enter the compromise, and the decree was binding on the client; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A lawyer's authority to act includes implied authority to compromise a case, unless the client expressly restricts or withdraws that authority. The lawyer must act in good faith and for the client's benefit; it is prudent and proper to consult the client when there is time and opportunity, and a client may impugn a compromise if available for consultation but bypassed. The Court followed Sourendra Nath v. Tarubala Dasi, AIR 1930 PC 158, approved Jiwibai v. Ramjuvar, AIR 1947 Nag. 17, and approved Laxmidas Ranchhodas v. Savitabai, [1955] 57 BLR 988, S. S. Waiker v. L. S. Waiker, AIR 1960 Bom. 20, and C. S. Nayak v. A. N. Menon, AIR 1963 Ker. 213; it also referred to Rondel v. Worsley, [1969] 1 AC 191. The Court distinguished Sourindra v. Heramba, AIR 1923 PC 98, as not deciding a pleader's authority as distinct from an advocate's.

rule.if: court_case_challenging_counsel_compromise and counsel_engaged_for_client and not client_restricted_or_withdrew_authority and compromise_made_in_good_faith and compromise_for_client_benefit and (not consultation_opportunity or client_or_representative_consulted)

predicates.court_case_challenging_counsel_compromis: The proceeding challenges whether a compromise made by a client's counsel binds the client.
predicates.counsel_engaged_for_client: The client engaged the counsel to act in the case.
predicates.client_restricted_or_withdrew_authority: The client expressly restricted or withdrew counsel's authority to compromise the case.
predicates.compromise_made_in_good_faith: Counsel made the compromise honestly and without fraud or sharp practice.
predicates.compromise_for_client_benefit: Counsel made the compromise for the client's benefit.
predicates.consultation_opportunity: There was time and opportunity to consult the client before making the compromise.
predicates.client_or_representative_consulted: Counsel consulted the client or the client's representative about the compromise.

issues.definition: When counsel was engaged in a case challenging a counsel-made compromise, the client did not restrict or withdraw authority, the compromise was made in good faith for the client's benefit, and either consultation was not practicable or the client or a representative was consulted, the client is bound by the compromise.
